newsitem.title: UK: Cold over UK holiday leads to large natgas flex buys.
newsitem.headline: Cold over UK holiday leads to large natgas flex buys.

text.p: Changing weather over the U.K.'s bank holiday weekend led to a large volume of natural gas purchased on the flexibility mechanism, the market instrument designed to cope with demand swings and keep the gas pipeline system in balance, traders said on Tuesday.

Although there was no flexibility mechanism trade on Saturday or Sunday, on Monday the system purchased a maximum of 278,584,192 kiloWatt hours (kWh), or slightly over 9.5 million therms. It was not immediately clear if all of this was actually taken into the system.
Prices on Monday ranged from a low of 0.385 p/kWh (around 11.28 pence a therm) to 0.5447 p/kWh, or slightly over 15.96 pence a therm.

A trader said the activity was caused not so much by the cold, wet and even snowy weather that engulfed much of Britain over the holiday, but by the change from the unusually mild weather that immediately preceded it.
"It's the change that generates activity, not the temperature," he said.

He added that demand forecasts supplied to him by pipeline operator Transco for smaller sites which are not metered on a daily basis had increased by 30 percent between late afternoon on Sunday and the same time on Monday.

The flexibility mechanism bought again on Tuesday morning, with the system buying a maximum of 108,082,341 kWh, or around 3.17 million therms. But prices were in a much tighter range, between 0.4979 p/kWh and 0.4981 p/kWh, a trader said. This is approximately 14.59 pence to 14.60 pence a therm.
On the spot market on Tuesday morning, the balance of May was talked at around 10.60 pence a therm, with the day ahead discussed in a wide range between 11.00/12.50 pence a therm.
